section_insight:
Overall health is good: 209 files analyzed, average grade A- (91.3), 95% of files at A or B. No critical defects anywhere in the codebase. Debt is concentrated, not spread — 11 files (5%) sit at C or below, and they cluster in two areas: the db/ library layer and the coach/AI feature.

The single D-grade file is apps/web/src/lib/db/connection.ts (62.7). It fails on three dimensions simultaneously: cyclomatic complexity of 46, 6 levels of nesting, and 16.7% code duplication. It is also a high-churn hotspot (score 0.46), meaning it takes hits frequently despite already being the worst-structured file in the repo. This is the one file that warrants immediate attention.

The next tier (C- to C) are all in related infrastructure: coach/tools.ts (complexity 38, duplication 15.8%), lib/db/summary.ts (complexity 34, nesting 12 levels — deepest nesting in the codebase), lib/whoop/upsert.ts (complexity 36, duplication 19.9%), and api/chat/route.ts (nesting 9 levels). All four are also high-churn files. The pattern is the same across all of them: logic that grew organically without extraction, nested conditionals instead of early returns or helper functions.

useChatSend.ts deserves a callout: cyclomatic complexity of 61 is the highest single complexity score in the repo. It is a C+ rather than lower only because nesting is contained (5 levels) and there is no duplication. Still a refactor candidate.

Debt concentration by area: lib/ has 7 of the 11 troubled files (out of 74 total lib files, so ~9% degraded). api/ and components/ each have 2. Scripts and config files are clean.

No F grades, no critical defects. The structural problems are real but tractable — they are confined to a specific cluster of high-traffic backend files rather than being a systemic codebase-wide issue.
